Spurious

SPYUR-ee-us -- stress on the first syllable, SPYUR. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Spurious is false or fake; not genuine or well-founded.

The senator's speech leaned on a spurious statistic that no researcher could ever trace back to a real study.

Worked Example

A student notices his test scores rose during a week he happened to eat chocolate daily, and announces that chocolate makes people smarter.

His conclusion rests on a spurious connection: the link between chocolate and scores sounds plausible but is false -- not genuine, not well-founded. Spurious describes claims and arguments that wear a convincing surface over nothing.

How Spurious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bogus

bogus: fake; not what it pretends to be

false

false: not true or correct

fallacious

Antonyms

genuine

genuine: real and authentic

valid

valid: well-founded and logically sound

How Strong Is It? — false → spurious → fallacious

false vs. spurious

false vs. spurious: False is the plain, flat word -- a false statement is simply untrue, while a spurious one adds a layer of disguise: it is untrue while dressed up to look convincing.

fallacious vs. spurious

fallacious vs. spurious: Fallacious presses harder than spurious on the broken logic itself: a spurious claim is false beneath a plausible surface, while a fallacious argument is rotten in its very reasoning, built to mislead from the first step.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of spurious.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — spuri-

root — spuri-: illegitimate; false (Latin spurius 'illegitimate, false')

suffix — -ious

suffix — -ious: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Spurious uses the -ious variant of this unit's suffix family. Latin spurius meant 'illegitimate, false' -- something not what it claims to be -- so spurious means 'full of falseness': a claim, connection, or argument whose pedigree does not hold up when you check it.

Use the root in a new word: spuriously

Use the root in a new word: spuriously: The two events were spuriously linked in the headline, as if one had somehow caused the other.

Word Building

Word Choice

Spurious belongs with claims, arguments, statistics, and correlations: a spurious claim, a spurious connection, spurious reasoning. For fake physical goods -- a fake designer bag, fake money -- English prefers 'counterfeit'; save spurious for falsehoods of the mind and the page.
